title: NFL to take Packers running back Josh Jacobs off the exempt list Monday, with its inquiry still open
dek: He can practice and play from next week. The league has not closed its own investigation, so a suspension is still possible.
what: ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Friday 16 October, citing sources, that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list on Monday 19 October, and that the league's investigation stays open.

ESPN reports Jacobs was placed on the list on 30 August while the league looked into a 23 May incident at his home near Green Bay. On 10 September he pleaded no contest to battery and criminal destruction of property, according to ESPN. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000, and agreed to a deferred judgment on the property charge.

ESPN says the league's inquiry under its personal conduct policy is still going and that the league had not yet reviewed surveillance video noted in the criminal report. Jacobs can practice and play after the removal. ESPN reports he could still be suspended, and games already missed would count toward any penalty. His legal team said he "accepts responsibility for his actions."
This is a report from sources, and I did not find a league statement. The removal takes effect on Monday, so it had not happened when this was written.
why: The exempt list and the personal conduct policy let the league act before or apart from the courts, and a return to play with an open inquiry is the kind of step fans and rival teams' supporters read in opposite ways.
next: Monday's formal removal, whether the league announces discipline, and whether he plays in Week 7.

sources.label: ESPN: Packers' Josh Jacobs eligible to return next week amid probe
